name: Rhubarb (Rheum root)
short: A review of liver-injury cohorts names Rheum officinale among the main herbs involved. Others say long-term inappropriate use may harm kidneys and rhubarb may play a role in melanosis coli.
text: Rhubarb root contains anthraquinones, and a review lists it among the anthraquinone-containing herbs most commonly used that may play a role in melanosis coli, a condition of the colon; it describes long-term use of anthraquinone laxatives as a potential risk for this condition and cautions against long-term use in large doses. A review of rhubarb and the kidney says earlier studies show a kidney-protective effect, but that studies have also shown long-term inappropriate use may cause damage to kidney function; the abstract does not say whether that evidence is from humans or animals. A systematic review of 31 liver-injury case cohort studies, in which 1874 of 7511 cases were attributed to herbs, named Rheum officinale among the main herbs causing herb-induced liver injury; the abstract does not give the number of rhubarb cases. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
